    AI Overview
    You can get an automatic six-month extension to file your federal tax return by submitting IRS Form 4868 by April 15, moving your deadline to October 15, 2026. This extension only applies to filing paperwork, not paying taxes; you must estimate and pay any taxes owed by April 15 to avoid penalties and interest. 
    How to File an Extension 
    • IRS Free File: All taxpayers can use IRS Free File to request an extension for free, regardless of income.
    • Electronic Payment: Pay all or part of your estimated tax due using Direct Pay, a debit/credit card, or digital wallet, and select "Extension" as the reason, which automatically files the extension
      .
    • Tax Software: Use popular tax software providers (e.g., TurboTax, H&R Block, FreeTaxUSA) to e-file the extension.
    • Mail: Mail a paper Form 4868, postmarked by April 15. 
    Key Considerations 
    • Not an Extension to Pay: Failure to pay by April 15 can result in interest and penalties, even with an extension.
    • Automatic Extension: The extension is automatic upon filling out the form; you do not need to explain why you need it.
    • State Taxes: Most states have their own extension procedures, though many honor the federal extension.
    • Business Extensions: S-corps and partnerships may have different, earlier deadlines (e.g., March 16) for their specific tax forms. 
    Disclaimer: This information is for tax year 2025/2026, which is filed by April 15, 2026.

    How to file for a tax extension

    While you will get more time to file your return, an extension does not grant you more time to pay your taxes. To avoid possible penalties, you should estimate and pay your federal taxes by the due date.

    Learn the ways to request an extension:
    • Online using IRS Free File
    • When you pay your estimated tax bill
    • Using IRS Form 4868
    How to pay taxes in installments

    If you feel that you may not be able to pay your tax bill in full by the due date, you may be eligible to pay in installments. Learn more about the IRS' payment plans and what additional costs and fees you may have to pay.
